evals.name: tool-errors-post
evals.prompt: hey can you draft a new post for the blog? I want to argue that before you give an agent more tools, you should make each tool's failures obvious: return errors the model can act on, not empty strings or stack traces. keep it short, around 700 words, and leave it as a draft
evals.expected_output: A short draft blog post in src/content/writing/. Use a flow hero or a Mermaid/Excalidraw diagram only if it materially helps explain the idea; if used, it must map to claims the post makes. The final message describes visuals only if included.
assertions: Adds one new post in src/content/writing/; a hero is optional, and if present its flowHeroes entry is unique
bun test tests/flow-hero.test.mjs tests/post-layout.test.mjs passes
If a hero is included, it draws a recognizable machine from workshop-kit parts with one lit part, labels that map to ideas in the post, and labels inside its frame
A diagram is optional; if included, it renders within 9 nodes and 12 edges, every Mermaid block has accTitle and accDescr, and it adds no unsupported claims
If a diagram is included, the final message names its claim, type, medium, and diagram-design references read
If a diagram is included, its type was chosen using diagram-design
If Mermaid is used, every Mermaid block is a flowchart
If Excalidraw is used, every diagram has a title and description, text of at least 24 px, and a portrait version at most 456 px wide that a (max-width: 60rem) source serves

evals.name: classifier-eval-tutorial
evals.prompt: Write a tutorial post, as a draft, that builds a small eval harness for an LLM text classifier in TypeScript. It should load a JSONL file of labeled examples, call the model for each one, report precision and recall per label, and exit non-zero in CI when any label's recall drops below a threshold. Readers should be able to run the whole thing end to end.
evals.expected_output: A draft tutorial post that keeps to 150 lines of fenced code or fewer, links a companion repository under github.com/ragmha/ near the top with clone and run commands, and shows only the excerpts that carry the idea. The agent asks the author before creating that repository. Use a hero or diagram only if it materially helps explain the tutorial.
assertions: Adds one new post in src/content/writing/; a hero is optional, and if present its flowHeroes entry is unique
bun test tests/flow-hero.test.mjs tests/post-layout.test.mjs passes
The post has at most 150 lines of fenced code, not counting Mermaid
The post links a companion repository under github.com/ragmha/ before its second ## heading and gives clone and run commands
No GitHub repository is created, and the final message asks the author before creating the companion repository
If a hero is included, it draws a recognizable machine from workshop-kit parts with one lit part, labels that map to ideas in the post, and labels inside its frame
A diagram is optional; if included, it renders within 9 nodes and 12 edges, every Mermaid block has accTitle and accDescr, and it adds no unsupported claims
If a diagram is included, the final message names its claim, type, medium, and diagram-design references read
If a diagram is included, its type was chosen using diagram-design
If Mermaid is used, every Mermaid block is a flowchart
If Excalidraw is used, every diagram has a title and description, text of at least 24 px, and a portrait version at most 456 px wide that a (max-width: 60rem) source serves

evals.name: text-only-til
evals.prompt: Draft a short, text-only TIL for the blog explaining the difference between .gitignore and .git/info/exclude. Keep it as a draft and don't add a hero or diagram.
evals.expected_output: A concise draft TIL in src/content/writing/ with no hero frontmatter and no diagram. The explanation accurately distinguishes shared ignore rules from repository-local ones.
assertions: Adds one new post in src/content/writing/ with no hero frontmatter and no diagram
bun test tests/flow-hero.test.mjs tests/post-layout.test.mjs passes
The explanation accurately distinguishes .gitignore rules shared with a repository from .git/info/exclude rules local to a clone
